_comment: GRAND over the FULL Ancash DEM (9855 x 6958 px, ~69 Mpx). A deliberate repeat of grand_arequipa_full.json over different ground: every physics and layout criterion below is copied from it unchanged, so a difference in the answer is a difference in the terrain and not in the question. Ancash is the Cordillera Blanca and the Callejon de Huaylas -- far steeper and higher than Arequipa, median elevation 2,954 m against a 3-25 deg deployable band, which is why it is worth asking.
_comment_downsample: 4, matching grand_arequipa_full.json so the two are comparable and so this run's mask is pixel-aligned with the TAMBO one it will be combined with. Ancash is 69 Mpx against Arequipa's 129, and the estimator puts it at 2.92 GiB of anonymous memory at ds 4 / stride 5 against ~7.5 GiB available -- comfortable, unlike Arequipa which needed the cap raised. The cost of downsampling is unchanged: area is measured on the downsampled mask while capacity is measured at full resolution, so read areas as lower bounds.
_comment_rfi: none, and this is the ONE criterion that differs from grand_arequipa_full.json, which uses its 'arequipa' preset. That preset is five hand-curated circles around Arequipa city, Majes, Cerro Verde, La Joya and Mollendo -- specific places, not a transferable rule, and there is no Ancash preset. Inventing a five-circle Ancash list would inject a new assumption into a run whose entire purpose is comparison, so this run excludes nothing and says so. The size of the difference: Arequipa's zones cover about 3,500 km2 of a ~120,000 km2 box, so roughly 2.9%. Read Ancash's area as at most ~3% flattered relative to Arequipa's on this account. input/roads/ancash_SRTMGL1_places.geojson carries the real OSM settlements for this box; they are map context here, not an exclusion filter.
_comment_origin: Deliberately null: read from the DEM's own ModelTiepointTag. The crop configs carry the crop's corner, which is not this file's.
